task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: team-level trait reliability (split-half and cross-season persistence)
variance decomposition of defense vs opponent vs game-script effects
methodological_questions: What share of between-team variance in opponents' H2-H1 change is true defense-specific variance rather than sampling noise?
Is the effect stable across split halves of a season and across adjacent seasons, given roster and coaching turnover?
How can the defense's effect be separated from the opponent offense's own H2-H1 tendency, game script, garbage time, and substitution patterns?
Does 120 team-seasons give enough power to detect a modest reliability?
How should regression to the mean be handled when teams are selected for extreme H2-H1 suppression?
evidence_establishes: Nothing. The retrieval returned zero records, so no historical evidence was available for this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether this question, or a close variant, has been studied before.
Whether earlier H2-H1 persistence estimates were null, positive or artifactual.
Which designs or controls have failed before.
The expected size of the true team-level variance component.
own_inferences: The raw per-game H2-H1 difference in opponent scoring is very noisy (SD of roughly 8-12 points). The SE over about 82 games is about 1 point, or about 1.5 over a 41-game half. Unless the true between-team SD is at least about 0.5-1 point, split-half reliability will be low (roughly 0.1-0.3).

The H2-H1 change is mechanically tied to game script. Leading teams slow down and trailing teams speed up. Good defenses build leads, so a defense's apparent effect may reflect its own score state or rotations, not suppression.

A 'defense effect' on H2-H1 is confounded with the opponent offense's own H2-H1 tendency, with the defense's own H2 fatigue and rotation changes, and with coaching halftime adjustments. These need crossed opponent and defense adjustment.
Extreme team-seasons will regress toward the mean, so any leaderboard of best or worst H2-H1 suppressors will overstate persistence unless reliability is estimated out of sample.
Roster and coaching turnover make cross-season persistence a conservative test of a trait. Within-season split-half is the more favourable test, and a true trait should show up there first.
With 30 teams x 4 seasons, split-half reliability within a season is testable, but the cross-season test is weaker because of non-independence by team (about 90 adjacent pairs, clustered by team).
I expect an adequately powered result to be small or null, with a meaningful chance that apparent persistence comes from score-state artifacts.
uncertainties: The true team-level SD of the H2-H1 effect is unknown, so the power calculation rests on assumptions.
The outcome metric is not yet fixed (points per 100 possessions, eFG%, or play-type suppression), and the choice may change reliability.
It is unclear whether 'effect on opponents' means a raw split or an opponent-adjusted one.
Garbage-time definitions and possession counts per half depend on play-by-play quality, which I have not checked.
Whether playoffs and the partial pre-completion 2025-26 data would be used is unspecified. Playoff samples per team are small and uneven.
I did not consult the glossary or data catalog, so field-level availability, such as possessions per half and matchup data, is assumed.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no records, so history neither supported nor changed the decision. The decision rests on my own reasoning about noise, confounding and power. No prior work is assumed.

blocking_constraints.text: With 120 team-seasons and about 41 games per half-sample, only moderate reliability (about 0.3 or higher) is detectable. A smaller true trait would give an inconclusive result.
The per-game H2-H1 difference is very noisy, so the reliability ceiling is probably low. The trait claim needs a pre-specified reliability threshold.

prior_work.summary: No [prior work] were retrieved, so it is unknown whether this has been studied by this project. No earlier finding is relied on.

risks.text: Opponent offense H2-H1 tendency, game script (leading or trailing), pace, rest, home/away, and the defense's own rotations and fatigue can all produce an H2-H1 change that is not a defensive effect.
H2 scoring depends on the H1 score state, which is itself shaped by defensive quality. Conditioning on or controlling for score state can induce bias.
Difference scores (H2 minus H1) have lower reliability than their components, and the noise per game is large.
There are only 30 teams per season. Cross-season pairs are clustered by team and the effective sample is small.
Selecting extreme teams for 'best' or 'avoid' lists inflates apparent persistence unless the evaluation is out of sample.
Roster, coaching and league-wide rule or pace changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 weaken cross-season stability. The league-wide H2-H1 baseline may also shift by season.
Garbage time, blowouts and overtime compress or distort H2 scoring. Teams that lead big mechanically show suppressed H2 opponent change.
Multiple outcome metrics, splits, and half definitions would inflate false positives if not pre-specified.
Using full-season adjustment factors, such as opponent ratings, to evaluate early or half-season data would leak information across the split. Adjustment must be computed within each split.

design.estimand: Team-level reliability of a defense's opponent-adjusted H2-H1 effect. Per game and team, compute opponent points per 100 possessions in H2 (periods 3-4) minus H1 (periods 1-2). Remove the opponent offense's season-level H2-H1 tendency and game covariates (home/away, rest, pre-game rating difference, pace) using a crossed model with defense and opponent random effects. The defense effect is the team random intercept. Primary reliability metrics are (a) Spearman-Brown corrected odd/even game split-half correlation within season and (b) adjacent-season correlation of the effect.
design.unit: Team-season (30 teams x 4 seasons = 120). For the cross-season analysis, adjacent team-season pairs (about 90) with cluster bootstrap by team.
design.sample: Regular season games only, 2022-23 through 2025-26 (2025-26 complete from 2026-04-13). Exclude overtime periods from the metric and exclude garbage time (pre-specified: margin of 20 or more with under 6 minutes left in Q4, plus possessions with both teams' bench units). Playoffs are a separate secondary descriptive analysis only, not pooled.
design.power: Under the hypothesis of a true reliability of 0.3, a split-half test over 120 team-seasons has about 85-90% power at alpha 0.05. For the adjacent-season correlation with n of about 90 pairs, power to detect r = 0.3 is about 0.85 and to detect r = 0.2 is about 0.5. Anything below r = 0.2 cannot be separated from zero. Run a simulation using the empirical per-game H2-H1 SD before locking the plan.
design.controls: Opponent offense H2-H1 baseline, home/away, rest days, pre-game team rating difference, pace, half-time score margin (sensitivity analysis only, given the outcome-derived concern), starter minutes in H2, and season fixed effects. Compute all adjustment factors within each split (no cross-split leakage). Report results with and without the margin control.
design.falsification: (1) Permutation null: randomly permute defense labels across games within season to get the null distribution of reliability. (2) Placebo split: assign games to halves at random (not odd/even) and check that reliability is stable. (3) Negative control: the same reliability computed on H2-H1 change in the defense's own team offense scoring (not attributable to the defense) and on a within-quarter placebo contrast such as Q2-Q1 and Q4-Q3, to see whether H2-H1 carries any signal beyond generic quarter-to-quarter noise. (4) A shuffled-season test to confirm that cross-season correlation exceeds that between unrelated teams.
design.multiplicity: One primary outcome (adjusted opponent points per 100 possessions H2-H1) and one primary reliability statistic (split-half Spearman-Brown, pooled across seasons). The adjacent-season correlation is a pre-specified key secondary. All other metrics (eFG%, turnover rate, play-type breakdowns) are exploratory and Holm-corrected, labeled as such.
design.decision_rule: Supported (reliable trait) if pooled split-half reliability is at least 0.30 with the 95% cluster-bootstrap CI lower bound above 0.15, the adjacent-season correlation is above 0.20 with CI excluding 0, and results survive the margin-control and garbage-time sensitivity analyses and the permutation null. Rejected if the upper CI bounds are below 0.15 (split-half) and 0.20 (cross-season). Otherwise inconclusive. If reliability disappears once score state or the opponent baseline is controlled, classify as an artifact.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, rotation and box-score files for 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons, as available on 2026-10-06 (2025-26 regular season complete as of 2026-04-13). Freeze the data snapshot and record file hashes. Pre-register the garbage-time definition, covariates, and thresholds before any reliability computation.
